subproblems.title: Euclidean coefficient norm of covectors under pull-back and interior product (parent (L0)–(L2))
subproblems.statement: For all N, N', k ∈ ℕ, writing |α| for covectorEuclideanNorm α (the Euclidean norm of the values of a covector on the strictly increasing tuples of standard basis vectors), |v| for the Euclidean norm and ‖A‖ for the operator norm: (L1) for every continuous linear map A : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} and every k-covector β on ℝ^{N'}, the pull-back A^#β := β.compContinuousLinearMap A, (A^#β)(w_1, …, w_k) = β(Aw_1, …, Aw_k), satisfies |A^#β| ≤ ‖A‖^k·|β|; (L2) for every v ∈ ℝ^N and every (k+1)-covector β on ℝ^N, the interior product ι_vβ := β.curryLeft v, (ι_vβ)(w_1, …, w_k) = β(v, w_1, …, w_k), satisfies |ι_vβ| ≤ |v|·|β|.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (N N' k : ℕ) (A : Euclid N →L[ℝ] Euclid N') (β : Covector (Euclid N') k), covectorEuclideanNorm (β.compContinuousLinearMap A) ≤ ‖A‖ ^ k * covectorEuclideanNorm β) ∧ ∀ (N k : ℕ) (v : Euclid N) (β : Covector (Euclid N) (k + 1)), covectorEuclideanNorm (β.curryLeft v) ≤ ‖v‖ * covectorEuclideanNorm β
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 1 ((L0)–(L2), Simon Ch. 6 §1), specialized and completed. No hypotheses and no sibling results are used.

Notation. e_1, …, e_N is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^N = Euclid N (EuclideanSpace.basisFun). For a k-covector α on ℝ^N, |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_J α(e_{J(1)}, …, e_{J(k)})²)^{1/2}, the sum over the strictly increasing J : Fin k → Fin N. |α| is the Euclidean norm of the coefficient vector (α(e_J))_J, which depends linearly on α, so |cα| = |c|·|α|. For an orthonormal basis f = (f_1, …, f_N) of ℝ^N and a k-multilinear map γ : (ℝ^N)^k → ℝ put S_f(γ) := Σ_{I : Fin k → Fin N} γ(f_{I(1)}, …, f_{I(k)})² (all index tuples). ‖A‖ is the operator norm and |v| the Euclidean norm.

1. Basis independence of S. Let f, f' be orthonormal bases of ℝ^N and γ k-multilinear. Write f_i = Σ_a O_{ai} f'_a with O_{ai} := ⟨f'_a, f_i⟩. O is an orthogonal matrix, so Σ_i O_{ai} O_{bi} = δ_{ab}. By multilinearity, γ(f_{I(1)}, …, f_{I(k)}) = Σ_{a ∈ [N]^k} (Π_m O_{a_m I(m)}) γ(f'_{a_1}, …, f'_{a_k}). Squaring and summing over I gives S_f(γ) = Σ_{a,b ∈ [N]^k} γ(f'_a) γ(f'_b) Π_m (Σ_i O_{a_m i} O_{b_m i}) = Σ_{a,b} γ(f'_a) γ(f'_b) Π_m δ_{a_m b_m} = S_{f'}(γ).

2. (L0) For an alternating k-covector α and every orthonormal basis f, S_f(α) = k!·|α|². By step 1 it suffices to take f = e. If I takes some value twice, then α(e_I) = 0. Every injective I : Fin k → Fin N factors uniquely as I = J∘σ with J strictly increasing and σ a permutation of Fin k, and α(e_{J∘σ}) = sign(σ)·α(e_J). Hence S_e(α) = Σ_J Σ_σ α(e_J)² = k!·|α|². (For k = 0 both sides equal the square of the single value of α, and 0! = 1.)

3. One-slot estimate. Let A : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} be continuous linear, e' the standard basis of ℝ^{N'} and β a k-covector on ℝ^{N'}. For 0 ≤ j ≤ k let γ_j(w_1, …, w_j, u_{j+1}, …, u_k) := β(Aw_1, …, Aw_j, u_{j+1}, …, u_k) (w's in ℝ^N, u's in ℝ^{N'}) and T_j := Σ γ_j(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(j)}, e'_{I(j+1)}, …, e'_{I(k)})², the sum over I(1), …, I(j) ∈ [N] and I(j+1), …, I(k) ∈ [N']. Claim: T_j ≤ ‖A‖²·T_{j−1} for 1 ≤ j ≤ k. Fix all indices except the j-th. The map u ↦ γ_{j−1}(…, u (in slot j), …) is a linear functional on ℝ^{N'}, hence of the form u ↦ ⟨g, u⟩ for some g ∈ ℝ^{N'}, and γ_j(…, e_i (in slot j), …) = ⟨g, Ae_i⟩. Then Σ_{i ∈ [N]} ⟨g, Ae_i⟩² = Σ_i ⟨A*g, e_i⟩² = |A*g|² ≤ ‖A*‖²|g|² = ‖A‖²·Σ_{i' ∈ [N']} ⟨g, e'_{i'}⟩² = ‖A‖²·Σ_{i'} γ_{j−1}(…, e'_{i'}, …)². Summing over the fixed indices proves the claim.

4. (L1) A^#β := β.compContinuousLinearMap A is an alternating k-covector on ℝ^N with A^#β(w_1, …, w_k) = β(Aw_1, …, Aw_k). By step 2, T_0 = S_{e'}(β) = k!·|β|² and T_k = S_e(A^#β) = k!·|A^#β|². Iterating step 3, T_k ≤ ‖A‖^{2k}·T_0, so |A^#β|² ≤ ‖A‖^{2k}|β|², and taking square roots of nonnegative numbers gives covectorEuclideanNorm (β.compContinuousLinearMap A) ≤ ‖A‖^k · covectorEuclideanNorm β. (For k = 0, A^#β = β and ‖A‖^0 = 1.)

5. (L2) Let v ∈ ℝ^N and β a (k+1)-covector on ℝ^N. ι_vβ := β.curryLeft v is the k-covector with ι_vβ(w_1, …, w_k) = β(v, w_1, …, w_k) (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft_apply_apply; Matrix.vecCons v w = Fin.cons v w), and it is linear in v. If v = 0 then ι_vβ = 0 and both sides are 0. Otherwise put f_1 := v/|v|; then ι_vβ = |v|·ι_{f_1}β, and by homogeneity of |·| it suffices to show |ι_{f_1}β| ≤ |β|. Extend f_1 to an orthonormal basis f = (f_1, …, f_N) of ℝ^N (Gram–Schmidt; Mathlib Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension). By step 2 in the basis f: k!·|ι_{f_1}β|² = Σ_{I ∈ [N]^k} β(f_1, f_{I(1)}, …, f_{I(k)})² and (k+1)!·|β|² = Σ_{I' ∈ [N]^{k+1}} β(f_{I'(0)}, …, f_{I'(k)})². In the second sum keep only the tuples I' in which the index 1 occurs exactly once (the dropped terms are ≥ 0). Such an I' is determined by the position p ∈ {0, …, k} of the index 1 and the tuple I ∈ ([N]∖{1})^k of the remaining entries in order, and β(f_{I'}) = ±β(f_1, f_I) (moving f_1 to the front permutes the arguments). Hence (k+1)!·|β|² ≥ (k+1)·Σ_{I ∈ ([N]∖{1})^k} β(f_1, f_I)² = (k+1)·Σ_{I ∈ [N]^k} β(f_1, f_I)² (a term with some I(m) = 1 vanishes because β is alternating) = (k+1)·k!·|ι_{f_1}β|². Dividing by (k+1)! gives |ι_{f_1}β|² ≤ |β|², hence |ι_vβ| ≤ |v|·|β|.

Steps 4 and 5 are the two conjuncts. ∎

(L0): S_f(α) = k!·|α|² for alternating α.
One-slot estimate T_j ≤ ‖A‖²T_{j−1}; iterating k times gives (L1).

subproblems.title: Gram-determinant bound for covector evaluations and norming covectors of orthonormal frames (parent (L0), (L3); reused accepted covectorEuclideanNorm_gram_bounds)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ: (i) for every n-covector α on ℝ^P and all v_1, …, v_n ∈ ℝ^P, |α(v_1, …, v_n)| ≤ |α|·√det(⟨v_a, v_b⟩)_{a,b}; (ii) for every orthonormal family τ_1, …, τ_n in ℝ^P there is an n-covector α with |α| ≤ 1 and α(τ_1, …, τ_n) = 1 (|α| = covectorEuclideanNorm α). This is the exact type of the accepted declaration covectorEuclideanNorm_gram_bounds, reused verbatim.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), (∀ (α : Covector (Euclid P) n) (v : Fin n → Euclid P), |α v| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α * Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (v i) (v j)))) ∧ ∀ τ : Fin n → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ τ → ∃ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ 1 ∧ α τ = 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 1 ((L0) and (L3): the Hilbert–Schmidt identity and the Jacobian identity |Λ_nA(e)| = √det(AᵀA) for unit simple n-vectors), specialized to the exact statement. (This accepted declaration is reused verbatim; the proof below proves its exact statement from scratch.)

Notation. e_1, …, e_P is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{J strictly increasing} α(e_J)²)^{1/2} for an n-covector α; for an orthonormal basis f of ℝ^P and an n-multilinear γ put S_f(γ) := Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} γ(f_{I(1)}, …, f_{I(n)})². Gram(v) := (⟨v_a, v_b⟩)_{a,b ≤ n}.

1. Basis independence. For orthonormal bases f, f' and n-multilinear γ, S_f(γ) = S_{f'}(γ): write f_i = Σ_a O_{ai}f'_a with O orthogonal, expand by multilinearity and use Σ_i O_{ai}O_{bi} = δ_{ab} (exactly as in the Hilbert–Schmidt computation: S_f(γ) = Σ_{a,b} γ(f'_a)γ(f'_b) Π_m Σ_i O_{a_m i}O_{b_m i} = S_{f'}(γ)).

2. (L0) For alternating α, S_f(α) = n!·|α|² for every orthonormal basis f: by step 1 take f = e; tuples with a repeated index contribute 0, and each injective I is uniquely J∘σ with J strictly increasing, σ a permutation, α(e_{J∘σ}) = sign(σ)α(e_J); so S_e(α) = n!·Σ_J α(e_J)². (n = 0: both sides are the square of the constant value, 0! = 1.)

3. (L3) If τ_1, …, τ_n are orthonormal, then |α(τ)| ≤ |α|. They are linearly independent, so n ≤ P, and they extend to an orthonormal basis f with f_m = τ_m for m ≤ n (Gram–Schmidt; Mathlib Orthonormal.exists_orthonormalBasis_extension). Among the tuples I in S_f(α) are the n! permutations σ of {1, …, n}, each contributing α(τ_{σ(1)}, …, τ_{σ(n)})² = (sign σ·α(τ))² = α(τ)²; the other terms are ≥ 0. So n!·|α|² = S_f(α) ≥ n!·α(τ)².

4. First conjunct: |α(v)| ≤ |α|·√det Gram(v) for all v_1, …, v_n ∈ ℝ^P. If v_1, …, v_n are linearly dependent, α(v) = 0 (an alternating multilinear map vanishes on linearly dependent families, Mathlib AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent), so the left side is 0 and the right side is ≥ 0 (det Gram(v) ≥ 0, Real.sqrt ≥ 0). Otherwise let τ_1, …, τ_n be an orthonormal basis of span(v_1, …, v_n) (Gram–Schmidt) and C the n×n matrix C_{ab} := ⟨τ_a, v_b⟩, so v_b = Σ_a C_{ab}τ_a. By multilinearity and alternation, α(v) = Σ_{a ∈ [n]^n} (Π_b C_{a_b b}) α(τ_{a_1}, …, τ_{a_n}) = det(C)·α(τ). Moreover Gram(v)_{bc} = ⟨v_b, v_c⟩ = Σ_a C_{ab}C_{ac} = (CᵀC)_{bc}, so det Gram(v) = det(C)², i.e. |det C| = √det Gram(v). With step 3, |α(v)| = |det C|·|α(τ)| ≤ √det Gram(v)·|α|.

5. Second conjunct. Let τ be orthonormal and define α_τ(w_1, …, w_n) := det(⟨τ_a, w_b⟩)_{a,b}. It is multilinear in w (the b-th column depends linearly on w_b), alternating (two equal w's give two equal columns), and continuous (finite dimension), hence an n-covector. α_τ(τ) = det(⟨τ_a, τ_b⟩) = det(I) = 1. Extend τ to an orthonormal basis f as in step 3. Then ⟨τ_a, f_j⟩ = δ_{aj} for j ≤ n and 0 for j > n, so for I ∈ [P]^n the matrix (⟨τ_a, f_{I(b)}⟩)_{a,b} has a zero column if some I(b) > n, a repeated column if I is not injective, and otherwise is the permutation matrix of I, with determinant sign(I). Hence S_f(α_τ) = n!, and by step 2 |α_τ|² = 1, so covectorEuclideanNorm α_τ = 1 ≤ 1 and α_τ(τ) = 1. (n = 0: α_τ is the constant 1, |α_τ| = 1.) ∎
proof_key_steps: Basis independence of Hilbert–Schmidt sums and (L0) S_f(α) = n!|α|².
(L3): |α(τ)| ≤ |α| for orthonormal τ via an orthonormal basis extending τ.
Gram bound: dependent families give 0; otherwise α(v) = det(C)α(τ) with det(C)² = det Gram(v).

Source: parent proof, step 4 (A2, the product with [[0,1]], Simon Ch. 6, 2.17–2.22, in the parent's t-integral form), with step 2 (A0) and the Conventions; the sibling dimred_mbl_dt_lp_covector_bounds supplies (L1) |A^#β| ≤ ‖A‖^k|β| and (L2) |ι_vβ| ≤ |v||β|. (VO) and (REP) are the two antecedents of the statement.

Notation. Currents are on univ: 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) = GeometricCurrentOn univ k, 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) = TestFormOn univ k. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α, ‖ω‖ := sup_y|ω(y)| (finite for a test form). ι(t, x) := (t, x_1, …, x_N) ∈ ℝ^{N+1} (Lean WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x))), e₀ := (1, 0, …, 0) (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1), Jv := ι(0, v), tail(y) := (y_1, …, y_N). J is linear and isometric (‖J‖ ≤ 1), |e₀| = 1, ι(t, x) = t·e₀ + Jx, ι is a closed isometric embedding of ℝ × ℝ^N, the derivative of x ↦ ι(t, x) is J and that of t ↦ ι(t, x) is e₀. NC X means: spt X compact, M(X) < ∞ and boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞ (= M(∂X) for degree ≥ 1).

0. Elementary facts.
 (a) |·| is a norm on k-covectors (the coefficient map α ↦ (α(e_J))_J is linear and injective), so |α + β| ≤ |α| + |β|, |−α| = |α|.
 (b) For every current T and test form ω, |T(ω)| ≤ M(T)·‖ω‖: trivial if M(T) = ∞; otherwise for ε > 0 the forms ±ω/(‖ω‖ + ε) are admissible for M(T) = M_{ℝ^N}(T) (tsupport ⊆ univ, pointwise norm ≤ 1), so ±T(ω) ≤ (‖ω‖ + ε)M(T); let ε ↓ 0. Conversely, if L is a linear functional on 𝒟^k with |L(ω)| ≤ C‖ω‖ for all ω, then L is a current (if ω_j → 0 in the test-form topology, the 0-th derivatives converge uniformly, so ‖ω_j‖ → 0 and L(ω_j) → 0) and M(L) ≤ C (every admissible ω has ‖ω‖ ≤ 1).
 (c) Support. spt T = ℝ^N ∖ Z_T, where Z_T is the (open) union of the open sets with compact closure on which T vanishes; spt T is closed. (S1) If E ⊆ ℝ^N is closed and T(ω) = 0 for every ω with tsupport ω ∩ E = ∅, then spt T ⊆ E: a point x ∉ E has an open ball B ∋ x with compact closure disjoint from E; every ω with tsupport ω ⊆ B satisfies T(ω) = 0, so x ∈ Z_T. (S2) spt(X − Y) ⊆ spt X ∪ spt Y (if x ∉ spt X ∪ spt Y, choose open W_1, W_2 ∋ x with compact closures on which X, resp. Y vanish; X − Y vanishes on W_1 ∩ W_2, whose closure is compact), and spt ∂X ⊆ spt X (if X vanishes on W so does ∂X, since tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω, SimonGMT tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). Also M(X − Y) ≤ M(X) + M(Y): for admissible ω, (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) + Y(−ω) and −ω is admissible. Hence for NC X, Y the current X − Y has compact support (closed subset of spt X ∪ spt Y) and finite mass; for X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1} with compact support and M(X), M(∂X) < ∞, ∂X has compact support and finite mass.
 (d) (A0) If M(X) < ∞, then for every open W with compact closure M_W(X) ≤ M(X) < ∞, so (REP) with U = ℝ^N (open) gives a Borel measure μ_X and ξ_X : ℝ^N → MultiVector with μ_X(W) = M_W(X) for open W (in particular μ_X(ℝ^N) = M(X) < ∞), ξ_X μ_X-a.e. strongly measurable, |ξ_X(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, and X(ω) = ∫ ξ_X(x)(ω(x)) dμ_X(x) for every test form ω.
 (e) Pointwise algebra (sibling, (L1), (L2)). For a (k+1)-covector α on ℝ^{N+1} put α₁ := (ι_{e₀}α)∘J^{×k}, i.e. α₁(v_1, …, v_k) = α(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_k) (Lean: (α.curryLeft e₀).compContinuousLinearMap J). α ↦ α₁ is continuous linear and |α₁| ≤ ‖J‖^k|ι_{e₀}α| ≤ |e₀|·|α| = |α|. For a k-covector α on ℝ^{N+1} put α_J := α∘J^{×k} (α.compContinuousLinearMap J); |α_J| ≤ |α|.

1. Slice forms. For ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) and t ∈ ℝ let η^ω_t(x) := (ω(ι(t, x)))₁, i.e. η^ω_t(x)(v) = ω(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_k). For a k-form ω on ℝ^{N+1} and s ∈ ℝ let β^ω_s(x) := (ω(ι(s, x)))_J, i.e. β^ω_s(x)(v) = ω(ι(s, x))(Jv_1, …, Jv_k). Each of these is a test form on ℝ^N: it is C^∞ in x (ω composed with the affine map x ↦ ι(t, x), followed by a fixed continuous linear map), and it vanishes outside the compact set {x : ι(t, x) ∈ tsupport ω} (preimage of a compact set under the closed isometric embedding x ↦ ι(t, x)), so it has compact support. Moreover ω ↦ η^ω_t and ω ↦ β^ω_s are linear; ‖η^ω_t‖ ≤ ‖ω‖ and ‖β^ω_s‖ ≤ ‖ω‖ by 0(e); and t ↦ η^ω_t is continuous for ‖·‖: ‖η^ω_t − η^ω_s‖ ≤ sup_x|ω(ι(t, x)) − ω(ι(s, x))| → 0 as s → t, because ω is uniformly continuous (continuous with compact support) and |ι(t, x) − ι(s, x)| = |t − s|. The same holds for t ↦ β^ω_t and, for ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N+1}), for t ↦ ∂_tβ^ω_t, where ∂_tβ^ω_t(x) := (D_{e₀}ω(ι(t, x)))_J (Dω is uniformly continuous); ∂_tβ^ω_t is again a test form, and for each x, v the function t ↦ β^ω_t(x)(v) is C^1 with derivative ∂_tβ^ω_t(x)(v).

2. Definition and (C3). For X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with compact support and M(X) < ∞ define cyl(X)(ω) := ∫_0^1 X(η^ω_t) dt for ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}); for all other X put cyl(X) := 0. The integrand t ↦ X(η^ω_t) is continuous (|X(η^ω_t) − X(η^ω_s)| ≤ M(X)‖η^ω_t − η^ω_s‖ by 0(b) and step 1), so the integral exists; cyl(X) is linear in ω and |cyl(X)(ω)| ≤ ∫_0^1 M(X)‖η^ω_t‖ dt ≤ M(X)‖ω‖. By 0(b), cyl(X) ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) and M(cyl X) ≤ M(X). For NC X and ω, the family η := (t ↦ η^ω_t) consists of test forms with η t x v = ω(ι(t, x))(Fin.cons e₀ (J ∘ v)) for all t, x, v, and cyl(X)(ω) = ∫_0^1 X(η t) dt: this is (C3).

3. Linearity (C2). For NC X, Y, X − Y has compact support and finite mass (0(c)), so by definition and linearity of the integral of continuous functions, cyl(X − Y)(ω) = ∫_0^1 (X(η^ω_t) − Y(η^ω_t)) dt = cyl(X)(ω) − cyl(Y)(ω) = (cyl X − cyl Y)(ω) (currents subtract pointwise), and GeometricCurrentOn.ext gives cyl(X − Y) = cyl X − cyl Y.

4. Support (C1, support part). Let X be NC and ω a test form with tsupport ω ∩ ι([0,1] × spt X) = ∅. For t ∈ [0,1], tsupport η^ω_t ⊆ {x : ι(t, x) ∈ tsupport ω} (the latter is closed and η^ω_t vanishes off it), which is disjoint from spt X; so X(η^ω_t) = 0 by (VO), and cyl(X)(ω) = 0. The set ι([0,1] × spt X) is compact, hence closed, so (S1) gives spt cyl(X) ⊆ ι([0,1] × spt X) = {y : ∃ t ∈ [0,1], ∃ x ∈ spt X, y = ι(t, x)}; spt cyl(X) is closed and contained in a compact set, hence compact.

5. Boundary formula. Let X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^N) have compact support with M(X) < ∞ and M(∂X) < ∞, and let ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}). Fix t, x and v_1, …, v_{k+1}. The coordinate formula for the exterior derivative (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_apply, ω being smooth) with w_0 = e₀, w_i = Jv_i gives
  dω(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_{k+1}) = D[ω(·)(Jv_1, …, Jv_{k+1})](ι(t, x))(e₀) + Σ_{i=1}^{k+1} (−1)^i D[ω(·)(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_{i−1}, Jv_{i+1}, …, Jv_{k+1})](ι(t, x))(Jv_i).
 The first term is ∂_tβ^ω_t(x)(v). Since the derivative of x ↦ ι(t, x) is J, D[g](ι(t, x))(Jv_i) = D[g∘ι(t, ·)](x)(v_i) for every differentiable g, so the i-th term equals (−1)^i D[η^ω_t(·)(v_1, …, v_{i−1}, v_{i+1}, …, v_{k+1})](x)(v_i); and the coordinate formula on ℝ^N for the smooth k-form η^ω_t reads d(η^ω_t)(x)(v) = Σ_{i=1}^{k+1} (−1)^{i−1} D[η^ω_t(·)(v_1, …, v_{i−1}, v_{i+1}, …, v_{k+1})](x)(v_i). Hence, as test forms on ℝ^N,
  η^{dω}_t = ∂_tβ^ω_t − d(η^ω_t)   (*)
 and ∂cyl(X)(ω) = cyl(X)(dω) = ∫_0^1 X(∂_tβ^ω_t) dt − ∫_0^1 X(d η^ω_t) dt.
 Second integral: X(dη^ω_t) = ∂X(η^ω_t) (definition of ∂). By 0(c), ∂X has compact support and finite mass, so by the definition in step 2 (the slice forms of ω used for ∂X are the same η^ω_t), ∫_0^1 ∂X(η^ω_t) dt = cyl(∂X)(ω).
 First integral (A0, Fubini, fundamental theorem of calculus, as in the parent): by 0(d), X(∂_tβ^ω_t) = ∫ ξ_X(x)(∂_tβ^ω_t(x)) dμ_X(x). The function (t, x) ↦ ξ_X(x)(∂_tβ^ω_t(x)) is a.e. strongly measurable for (Lebesgue on [0,1]) ⊗ μ_X (ξ_X is a.e. strongly measurable, (t, x) ↦ ∂_tβ^ω_t(x) is continuous, and evaluation is continuous bilinear) and bounded by sup|Dω| (|ξ_X(x)(α)| ≤ |α| and 0(e)); μ_X is finite, so Fubini applies: ∫_0^1 X(∂_tβ^ω_t) dt = ∫ (∫_0^1 ∂_t[ξ_X(x)(β^ω_t(x))] dt) dμ_X(x) (ξ_X(x) is linear and continuous, so it commutes with ∂_t) = ∫ (ξ_X(x)(β^ω_1(x)) − ξ_X(x)(β^ω_0(x))) dμ_X(x) (fundamental theorem of calculus for the C^1 function t ↦ ξ_X(x)(β^ω_t(x)), Mathlib intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt) = X(β^ω_1) − X(β^ω_0).
 Therefore ∂cyl(X)(ω) = X(β^ω_1) − X(β^ω_0) − cyl(∂X)(ω). With η₀ := β^ω_0, η₁ := β^ω_1 (test forms with η_s x v = ω(ι(s, x))(fun i => J(v i))) this is (C5).
 Degree 0 (C4): let X ∈ 𝒟_0(ℝ^N) have compact support and M(X) < ∞, and ω ∈ 𝒟^0(ℝ^{N+1}). Then η^{dω}_t(x) = dω(ι(t, x))(e₀) = ∂_t[ω(ι(t, x))] = ∂_tβ^ω_t(x) (only the first term of the coordinate formula occurs), so by the same Fubini/FTC computation ∂cyl(X)(ω) = X(β^ω_1) − X(β^ω_0), which is (C4) with η_s := β^ω_s (here v : Fin 0 → ℝ^N is empty and β^ω_s(x) is the 0-covector with value ω(ι(s, x))).

6. Boundary mass (C1, remaining part). Let X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) be NC. If k = 0, step 5 and 0(b) give |∂cyl(X)(ω)| ≤ |X(β^ω_1)| + |X(β^ω_0)| ≤ 2M(X)‖ω‖. If k = k' + 1, then M(∂X) < ∞ and step 5 with step 2 for ∂X gives |∂cyl(X)(ω)| ≤ (2M(X) + M(∂X))‖ω‖. By 0(b), M(∂cyl X) < ∞ in both cases. Together with steps 2 and 4 this proves (C1): spt cyl(X) is compact, M(cyl X) ≤ M(X), M(∂cyl X) < ∞, and spt cyl(X) ⊆ ι([0,1] × spt X).

Steps 2–6 prove the five conjuncts (C1)–(C5) for the operator cyl of step 2. ∎
proof_key_steps: Slice forms η^ω_t(x) = (ω(ι(t,x)))₁ and β^ω_s(x) = (ω(ι(s,x)))_J are test forms, linear in ω, with ‖·‖ ≤ ‖ω‖ by (L1), (L2), continuous in t.
cyl(X)(ω) := ∫_0^1 X(η^ω_t) dt is a current with M(cyl X) ≤ M(X); this gives (C3) and (C2).
Support: forms missing ι([0,1] × spt X) have slices missing spt X, so (VO) and (S1) give (C1)'s support bound.
Coordinate formula for d: η^{dω}_t = ∂_tβ^ω_t − d(η^ω_t); A0 (REP, VO), Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus give (C4), (C5).
The boundary formulas bound M(∂cyl X) by 2M(X) + M(∂X).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 2 (A0), 3 (A1, smooth push-forward), 5 (A3, smooth homotopy formula and mass estimate), 6 (A4, Lipschitz push-forward, incl. the cut-off homotopy of A4(f)) and the operator definitions of C1 (Simon Ch. 6, 2.23–2.29). The product with [[0,1]] (parent step 4, A2) is the sibling dimred_mbl_dt_lp_cylinder, whose operator is re-exported as cyl; the sibling dimred_mbl_dt_lp_covector_bounds supplies (L1) |A^#β| ≤ ‖A‖^k|β| and (L2) |ι_vβ| ≤ |v||β|. (VO) and (REP) are the antecedents of the statement (and of the cylinder sibling).

0. Conventions and elementary facts.
 (a) 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) = GeometricCurrentOn univ k, 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) = TestFormOn univ k. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α is the Euclidean norm of the coefficient vector (α(e_J))_{J increasing}; the coefficient map is linear and injective, so |·| is a norm on the finite-dimensional space of k-covectors (|α + β| ≤ |α| + |β|, |sα| = |s||α|, equivalent to the operator norm, |∫α_t dt| ≤ ∫|α_t| dt). ‖ω‖ := sup_x|ω(x)| < ∞ for test forms.
 (b) Mass. M_W(T) is the supremum of T(ω) over test forms with tsupport ⊆ W and pointwise norm ≤ 1, M := M_{ℝ^N}. For every current T and test form ω, |T(ω)| ≤ M(T)‖ω‖ (for ε > 0 the forms ±ω/(‖ω‖ + ε) are admissible). A linear functional L on test forms with |L(ω)| ≤ C‖ω‖ is a current (a sequence converging to 0 in the test-form topology converges to 0 uniformly) with M(L) ≤ C. If T_j → T weakly (T_j(ω) → T(ω) for all ω) then ∂T_j → ∂T weakly (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary) and M(T) ≤ liminf M(T_j) (WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf with W = univ).
 (c) Support. spt T is the complement of the open union Z_T of the open sets with compact closure on which T vanishes. (S1) If E is closed and T(ω) = 0 whenever tsupport ω ∩ E = ∅, then spt T ⊆ E. (S2) spt(X − Y) ⊆ spt X ∪ spt Y, and spt ∂X ⊆ spt X (tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω, SimonGMT tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). (S3) If test forms η, η' agree on an open W ⊇ spt X then X(η) = X(η'): tsupport(η − η') ⊆ ℝ^N ∖ W is disjoint from spt X, so (VO) gives X(η − η') = 0. (S4) If spt X = ∅ then X = 0 by (VO).
 (d) NC_k(ℝ^N) is the set of X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with IsCompact X.support, X.mass < ∞ and boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞ (= M(∂X) < ∞ for k ≥ 1; automatic for k = 0). NC_k is closed under differences: spt(X − Y) is closed and contained in the compact spt X ∪ spt Y; M(X − Y) ≤ M(X) + M(Y) since (X − Y)(ω) = X(ω) + Y(−ω); ∂(X − Y) = ∂X − ∂Y (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). If X ∈ NC_{k+1} then ∂X ∈ NC_k (spt ∂X ⊆ spt X, ∂∂X = 0 by SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary).
 (e) Cut-offs. For compact K ⊆ ℝ^N (or ℝ^{N+1}) and ε > 0 there is ζ ∈ C^∞_c with 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1, ζ = 1 on the open ε/2-neighbourhood of K and tsupport ζ inside the closed 2ε-neighbourhood of K: convolve the indicator of the closed ε-neighbourhood of K with a normalized smooth bump supported in the ball of radius ε/2 (Mathlib ContDiffBump.normed, HasCompactSupport.contDiff_convolution_left). In particular, if O is open and K ⊆ O, choosing ε with the 2ε-neighbourhood of K inside O (compactness) gives ζ = 1 on an open O' with K ⊆ O' ⊆ O.
 (f) Mollification. Fix normalized smooth bumps ϕ_σ ≥ 0 (σ > 0) supported in B_σ(0) with ∫ϕ_σ = 1. For a Λ-Lipschitz F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} put F_σ(x) := ∫ ϕ_σ(y)F(x − y) dy. F_σ is C^∞, |F_σ(x) − F_σ(x')| ≤ ∫ϕ_σ(y)|F(x − y) − F(x' − y)| dy ≤ Λ|x − x'| (so F_σ is Λ-Lipschitz and ‖DF_σ‖ ≤ Λ), and |F_σ(x) − F(x)| ≤ ∫ϕ_σ(y)|F(x − y) − F(x)| dy ≤ Λσ. The construction does not depend on Λ.
 (g) Coordinates on ℝ^{N+1}: ι(t, x) := (t, x_1, …, x_N) (WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.cons t (WithLp.ofLp x))), e₀ := ι(1, 0) (EuclideanSpace.single 0 1), Jv := ι(0, v), tail(y) := (y_1, …, y_N); J is linear isometric, ι(t, x) = te₀ + Jx, the derivative of x ↦ ι(t, x) is J and that of t ↦ ι(t, x) is e₀.
 (h) Smooth pull-back. For C^∞ F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} and a k-form ω on ℝ^{N'}, F^#ω(x) := ω(F(x))∘DF(x)^{×k} (Lean (ω (F x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ F x)). If ω is C^∞ so is F^#ω: x ↦ ω(F(x)) and x ↦ DF(x) are C^∞, and (α, A) ↦ α.compContinuousLinearMap A is the restriction to the diagonal of the continuous multilinear map (α, A_1, …, A_k) ↦ α∘(A_1 × ⋯ × A_k), hence a continuous polynomial map and C^∞ (its derivative is Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.hasStrictFDerivAt_compContinuousLinearMap; iterate, or use that bounded multilinear maps are C^∞); d(F^#ω) = F^#(dω) (SimonGMT exteriorDerivativeOn_pullbackFormWithin with U = V = ℝ^N, where fderivWithin on univ is fderiv); (G∘F)^#ω = F^#(G^#ω) (chain rule). For a (k+1)-covector β, linear A and vector w: ι_w(β∘A^{×(k+1)}) = (ι_{Aw}β)∘A^{×k}.

1. A0 (Representation). Let X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) with M(X) < ∞. For open W with compact closure M_W(X) ≤ M(X) < ∞, so (REP) with U = ℝ^N gives a Borel measure μ_X and ξ_X with μ_X(W) = M_W(X) for open W, ξ_X μ_X-a.e. strongly measurable, |ξ_X(x)(α)| ≤ |α|, and X(ω) = ∫ξ_X(x)(ω(x)) dμ_X(x). Then μ_X(ℝ^N) = M(X), and μ_X(ℝ^N ∖ spt X) = M_{ℝ^N∖spt X}(X) = 0 because every admissible form supported in the open set ℝ^N ∖ spt X is killed by (VO). Hence |X(η)| ≤ ∫_{spt X}|η(x)| dμ_X ≤ M(X)·sup_{x ∈ spt X}|η(x)| for every test form η.

2. A1 (Smooth push-forward). Let X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^N) have compact support and M(X) < ∞, and F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} be C^∞. Choose ζ as in 0(e) for K = spt X, ζ = 1 on an open W_ζ ⊇ spt X. For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N'}), ζF^#ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) (C^∞ by 0(h), tsupport ⊆ tsupport ζ compact); put F_#X(ω) := X(ζF^#ω). By (S3) this does not depend on ζ, and X(η) = F_#X(ω) for every test form η that equals F^#ω on an open set containing spt X.
 (a) Mass: by A0 (ζ = 1 on spt X) and (L1), |F_#X(ω)| ≤ sup_{x ∈ spt X}‖DF(x)‖^k·|ω(F(x))|·M(X) ≤ Λ_F^k M(X)‖ω‖ with Λ_F := sup_{spt X}‖DF‖ < ∞. F_#X is linear, hence (0(b)) a current with M(F_#X) ≤ Λ_F^k M(X).
 (b) Linearity in X: with one ζ equal to 1 near spt X ∪ spt Y ⊇ spt(X − Y), F_#(X − Y) = F_#X − F_#Y.
 (c) Boundary: if X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1} and M(∂X) < ∞, then ∂F_#X = F_#∂X: ∂F_#X(ω) = X(ζF^#dω), and ζF^#dω = ζ·d(F^#ω) agrees with d(ζF^#ω) on W_ζ (ζ ≡ 1 there), so by (S3) X(ζF^#dω) = X(d(ζF^#ω)) = ∂X(ζF^#ω) = F_#∂X(ω) (the last step by (S3) for ∂X, spt ∂X ⊆ spt X ⊆ W_ζ).
 (d) Support: spt F_#X ⊆ F(spt X): if tsupport ω ∩ F(spt X) = ∅, F^#ω vanishes on the open set F^{-1}(ℝ^{N'} ∖ tsupport ω) ⊇ spt X, so F_#X(ω) = X(0) = 0 by (S3); F(spt X) is compact, and (S1) applies.

3. The product with [[0,1]]. Apply the sibling dimred_mbl_dt_lp_cylinder (its antecedents are (VO), (REP)) and let cyl = cyl_{N,k} be its operator with: (C1) for NC X, spt cyl(X) is compact, M(cyl X) ≤ M(X), M(∂cyl X) < ∞, spt cyl(X) ⊆ ι([0,1] × spt X); (C2) cyl(X − Y) = cyl X − cyl Y for NC X, Y; (C3) for NC X and ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) there are test forms η_t (t ∈ ℝ) with η_t(x)(v) = ω(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_k) and cyl(X)(ω) = ∫_0^1 X(η_t) dt; (C4), (C5) the boundary formulas ∂cyl(X)(ω) = X(β_1) − X(β_0) (degree 0) and ∂cyl(X)(ω) = X(β_1) − X(β_0) − cyl(∂X)(ω) (degree k+1, compact support and M(X), M(∂X) < ∞), where β_s are test forms on ℝ^N with β_s(x)(v) = ω(ι(s, x))(Jv_1, …). In particular cyl(X) ∈ NC_{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) for X ∈ NC_k, and cyl(∂X) ∈ NC_k(ℝ^{N+1}) for X ∈ NC_{k+1} (0(d)).

4. A3 (Smooth homotopy formula). Let X ∈ NC_k(ℝ^N), F, G : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} C^∞ with ‖DF‖, ‖DG‖ ≤ Λ everywhere, and H : ℝ^{N+1} → ℝ^{N'} C^∞ with H(ι(t, x)) = F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)) for all ι(t, x) in an open set O ⊇ ι([0,1] × spt X). H_# denotes A1 in ℝ^{N+1}, applicable to cyl(X) and cyl(∂X) by step 3. By 0(e) applied in ℝ^{N+1} to the compact set ι([0,1] × spt X) ⊆ O, fix ζ̃ ∈ C^∞_c(ℝ^{N+1}) with ζ̃ = 1 on an open set O' with ι([0,1] × spt X) ⊆ O' ⊆ O; it is an admissible cut-off for A1 applied to cyl(X) and to cyl(∂X), whose supports lie in ι([0,1] × spt X) by (C1) and (S2). Then:
 (i) G_#X − F_#X = ∂H_#(cyl X) + H_#(cyl ∂X) for k ≥ 1, and G_#X − F_#X = ∂H_#(cyl X) for k = 0.
 Proof. By A1(c) in ℝ^{N+1} (cyl X has compact support, finite mass and finite boundary mass), ∂H_#(cyl X)(ω) = H_#(∂cyl X)(ω) = ∂cyl(X)(ζ̃H^#ω). By (C5) (resp. (C4) if k = 0) applied to the test form ζ̃H^#ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^{N+1}): ∂cyl(X)(ζ̃H^#ω) = X(β_1) − X(β_0) − cyl(∂X)(ζ̃H^#ω) (last term absent for k = 0), where β_s(x)(v) = (ζ̃H^#ω)(ι(s, x))(Jv_1, …, Jv_k). For s ∈ {0, 1} the open set W_s := {x : ι(s, x) ∈ O'} contains spt X, and for x ∈ W_s: ζ̃ = 1 near ι(s, x), H∘ι(s, ·) equals F (s = 0), resp. G (s = 1), near x, so DH(ι(s, x))J = DF(x), resp. DG(x), and β_0(x) = ω(F(x))∘DF(x)^{×k} = F^#ω(x), β_1(x) = G^#ω(x). By A1, X(β_0) = F_#X(ω) and X(β_1) = G_#X(ω). Finally cyl(∂X)(ζ̃H^#ω) = H_#(cyl ∂X)(ω) by the definition of A1 for cyl(∂X). Rearranging gives (i).
 (ii) M(H_#(cyl X)) ≤ δ₀·(2Λ)^k·M(X), δ₀ := sup_{x ∈ spt X}|G(x) − F(x)|.
 Proof. Put ω̃ := ζ̃H^#ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}). By A1 and (C3), H_#(cyl X)(ω) = cyl(X)(ω̃) = ∫_0^1 X(η_t) dt with η_t(x)(v) = ω̃(ι(t, x))(e₀, Jv_1, …, Jv_k). For x ∈ spt X and t ∈ [0,1], ω̃ = H^#ω near ι(t, x) ∈ O', and differentiating H(ι(t, x')) = F(x') + t(G(x') − F(x')) (valid near (t, x)) gives DH(ι(t, x))e₀ = G(x) − F(x) and DH(ι(t, x))J = (1 − t)DF(x) + tDG(x) =: A_t(x), ‖A_t(x)‖ ≤ Λ ≤ 2Λ. By 0(h), η_t(x) = (ι_{G(x)−F(x)}ω(H(ι(t, x))))∘A_t(x)^{×k}, so by (L1), (L2): |η_t(x)| ≤ (2Λ)^k·|G(x) − F(x)|·‖ω‖ ≤ (2Λ)^k δ₀‖ω‖ for x ∈ spt X. By A1's last estimate (A0), |X(η_t)| ≤ M(X)·sup_{spt X}|η_t| ≤ δ₀(2Λ)^kM(X)‖ω‖, hence |H_#(cyl X)(ω)| ≤ δ₀(2Λ)^kM(X)‖ω‖ and 0(b) gives (ii).

5. A4 (Lipschitz push-forward). Let X ∈ NC_k(ℝ^N), F : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} Λ-Lipschitz, F_σ as in 0(f).
 (E) For C^∞ F', G' : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} with ‖DF'‖, ‖DG'‖ ≤ Λ and δ' := sup_{spt X}|F' − G'|: |G'_#X(ω) − F'_#X(ω)| ≤ δ'((2Λ)^kM(X)‖dω‖ + (2Λ)^{k−1}M(∂X)‖ω‖) (second term absent for k = 0). Proof: fix s ∈ C^∞(ℝ) with s(t) = t on (−1, 2) and s, s' bounded (s(t) := t·b(t) with b smooth, b = 1 on [−1, 2], b = 0 outside (−2, 3)), and χ ∈ C^∞_c(ℝ^N), 0 ≤ χ ≤ 1, χ = 1 on an open W_χ ⊇ spt X (0(e)). H(y) := F'(tail y) + s(y_0)χ(tail y)(G' − F')(tail y) is C^∞ and equals F' + t(G' − F') on the open set ι((−1, 2) × W_χ) ⊇ ι([0,1] × spt X). By step 4(i), G'_#X(ω) − F'_#X(ω) = H_#(cyl X)(dω) + H_#(cyl ∂X)(ω); step 4(ii) for X and for ∂X ∈ NC_{k−1} (spt ∂X ⊆ spt X) together with 0(b) gives (E).
 (a) Existence and mass. For σ, τ > 0, sup|F_σ − F_τ| ≤ Λ(σ + τ), so by (E) (F_σ)_#X(ω) is Cauchy as σ ↓ 0; define F_#X(ω) := lim_{σ↓0}(F_σ)_#X(ω). By 2(a), |(F_σ)_#X(ω)| ≤ Λ^kM(X)‖ω‖, so |F_#X(ω)| ≤ Λ^kM(X)‖ω‖; F_#X is linear in ω, hence (0(b)) a current with M(F_#X) ≤ Λ^kM(X). F_#X does not depend on Λ.
 (b) Boundary. For X ∈ NC_{k+1}: ∂F_#X(ω) = F_#X(dω) = lim(F_σ)_#X(dω) = lim(F_σ)_#∂X(ω) = F_#∂X(ω) (2(c); ∂X ∈ NC_k).
 (c) Smooth maps. If F is C^∞ and Λ-Lipschitz, the A4 push-forward equals the A1 push-forward: by (E) with F' = F_σ, G' = F (δ' ≤ Λσ) the difference tends to 0. In particular id_#X(ω) = X(ζω) = X(ω) by (S3), i.e. id_#X = X.
 (d) Support. spt F_#X ⊆ F(spt X): if tsupport ω ∩ F(spt X) = ∅, these compact sets have positive distance d₀, and for Λσ < d₀, F_σ(spt X) ∩ tsupport ω = ∅, so (F_σ)_#X(ω) = 0 (argument of 2(d)); hence F_#X(ω) = 0 and (S1) applies.
 (e) Locality and linearity. If F, G are Λ-Lipschitz and |F − G| ≤ δ on spt X, then |F_#X(ω) − G_#X(ω)| ≤ δ((2Λ)^kM(X)‖dω‖ + (2Λ)^{k−1}M(∂X)‖ω‖): apply (E) to F_σ, G_σ (sup_{spt X}|F_σ − G_σ| ≤ δ + 2Λσ) and let σ ↓ 0. In particular F_#X = G_#X if F = G on spt X. For X, Y ∈ NC_k, (F_σ)_#(X − Y) = (F_σ)_#X − (F_σ)_#Y (2(b)); in the limit F_#(X − Y) = F_#X − F_#Y (X − Y ∈ NC_k by 0(d)).
 (f) Homotopy formula. Let F, G : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} be Λ-Lipschitz and H : ℝ^{N+1} → ℝ^{N'} Lipschitz with H(ι(t, x)) = F(x) + t(G(x) − F(x)) for x ∈ spt X, t ∈ [0,1]. Then G_#X − F_#X = ∂H_#(cyl X) + H_#(cyl ∂X) for k ≥ 1 (without the last term for k = 0), and M(H_#(cyl X)) ≤ δ(2Λ)^kM(X) whenever δ ∈ ℝ and |F − G| ≤ δ on spt X. (H_# is the A4 push-forward in ℝ^{N+1} of cyl X ∈ NC_{k+1} and cyl ∂X ∈ NC_k, step 3.)
 Proof. Independence of H: if H, H' are Lipschitz (with a common constant) and agree on ι([0,1] × spt X), which contains spt cyl(X) and spt cyl(∂X) ((C1), (S2)), then H_#Y = H'_#Y for Y = cyl X, cyl ∂X by (e) in ℝ^{N+1} with δ = 0. So it suffices to treat H_*(y) := F(tail y) + s(y_0)χ(tail y)(G − F)(tail y) (s, χ as in (E)), which agrees with F + t(G − F) on ι([0,1] × spt X) and is Lipschitz (uniform limit of the L₀-Lipschitz maps H_σ below). For σ ∈ (0, 1] put H_σ(y) := F_σ(tail y) + s(y_0)χ(tail y)(G_σ − F_σ)(tail y). It is C^∞; ∂_tH_σ = s'χ(G_σ − F_σ) and D_xH_σ = DF_σ + s[(G_σ − F_σ)⊗Dχ + χ(DG_σ − DF_σ)] are bounded uniformly in σ ≤ 1 (|G_σ − F_σ| ≤ |G − F| + 2Λ is bounded on the compact tsupport χ; ‖DF_σ‖, ‖DG_σ‖ ≤ Λ), so all H_σ are L₀-Lipschitz for one L₀; H_σ = F_σ + t(G_σ − F_σ) on ι((−1, 2) × W_χ) ⊇ ι([0,1] × spt X); and sup|H_σ − H_*| ≤ (1 + 2 sup|s|)Λσ. By step 4 for F_σ, G_σ, H_σ (A1 push-forwards, equal to A4 push-forwards by (c)): (G_σ)_#X − (F_σ)_#X = ∂(H_σ)_#(cyl X) + (H_σ)_#(cyl ∂X) and M((H_σ)_#(cyl X)) ≤ sup_{spt X}|G_σ − F_σ|(2Λ)^kM(X). Let σ = σ_j := 1/(j+1). The left side converges weakly to G_#X − F_#X (definition (a)); by (e) in ℝ^{N+1} (Lipschitz constant max(L₀, Lip H_*), δ = sup|H_σ − H_*| → 0), (H_σ)_#Y → (H_*)_#Y weakly for both Y; boundaries of weakly convergent sequences converge weakly (0(b)). The weak limits agree on every test form, so the currents are equal (GeometricCurrentOn.ext). For the mass: sup_{spt X}|G_σ − F_σ| ≤ δ + 2Λσ, and lower semicontinuity (0(b)) gives M((H_*)_#(cyl X)) ≤ δ(2Λ)^kM(X) when δ ≥ 0. If δ < 0 the hypothesis forces spt X = ∅, so X = 0 (S4), cyl X = 0 (by (C3) its value is ∫_0^1 0 dt) and its push-forward is 0; both sides vanish (ENNReal.ofReal δ = 0).

6. Definitions. lpush_{N,N',k}(F, X) := F_#X (A4) if F is Lipschitz for some constant and X ∈ NC_k(ℝ^N), and := 0 otherwise. cyl_{N,k} is the operator of step 3.

7. Verification of the twelve conjuncts (NC X means IsCompact X.support, X.mass < ∞, boundaryMassOn X univ < ∞; push-forwards of NC currents by Lipschitz maps are A4 push-forwards).
 (1) lpush N N k (fun x => x) X = X for NC X: A4(c).
 (2) lpush(F, X − Y) = lpush(F, X) − lpush(F, Y): A4(e); X − Y ∈ NC_k by 0(d).
 (3) EqOn F G (spt X) ⇒ lpush(F, X) = lpush(G, X): A4(e) with δ = 0.
 (4) Mass ≤ Λ^k·M(X) and support ⊆ F '' spt X: A4(a), A4(d).
 (5) X ∈ 𝒟_{k+1} with compact support and M(X), M(∂X) < ∞ is in NC_{k+1} and ∂X ∈ NC_k; A4(b).
 (6) Put F_j := F_{σ_j}, σ_j := 1/(j+1): C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞)), Λ-Lipschitz, sup|F_j − F| ≤ Λσ_j → 0, i.e. TendstoUniformly F_j F. Given ω, fix ζ as in 0(e) for spt X (ζ = 1 on an open W ⊇ spt X) and η_j := ζF_j^#ω ∈ 𝒟^k(ℝ^N). Then η_j = F_j^#ω on W, and X(η_j) = (F_j)_#X(ω) (A1) → F_#X(ω) = lpush(F, X)(ω) (A4(a)).
 (7) (C1): spt cyl(X) is compact, M(cyl X) ≤ M(X) < ∞, M(∂cyl X) < ∞, and spt cyl(X) ⊆ ι([0,1] × spt X) = {y : ∃ t ∈ [0,1], ∃ x ∈ spt X, y = ι(t, x)}.
 (8) cyl(X − Y) = cyl(X) − cyl(Y): (C2).
 (9) (C3) verbatim: for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}(ℝ^{N+1}) a family η : ℝ → 𝒟^k(ℝ^N) with η t x v = ω(ι(t, x))(Fin.cons e₀ (J∘v)) and cyl N k X ω = ∫_0^1 X(η t) dt.
 (10) Degree 0: X ∈ 𝒟_0 with compact support and finite mass is in NC_0; A4(f) with the given L-Lipschitz H gives lpush(G, X) − lpush(F, X) = ∂lpush(H, cyl(X)).
 (11) Degree k + 1: A4(f) gives lpush(G, X) − lpush(F, X) = ∂lpush(H, cyl(X)) + lpush(H, cyl(∂X)), which is the stated identity after subtracting lpush(H, cyl(∂X)) (currents subtract pointwise on test forms; GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
 (12) A4(f) mass bound, with ENNReal.ofReal δ = max(δ, 0). ∎
proof_key_steps: Conventions: mass/norm facts, support facts (S1)–(S4) from (VO), NC closure, cut-offs, mollifiers F_σ (C^∞, Λ-Lipschitz, |F_σ − F| ≤ Λσ), smooth pull-backs.
A0 from (REP), (VO): |X(η)| ≤ M(X) sup_{spt X}|η|.
A1: smooth push-forward F_#X(ω) = X(ζF^#ω): a current with mass ≤ sup‖DF‖^k M(X) (L1), linear, ∂F_#X = F_#∂X, spt ⊆ F(spt X).
cyl from the sibling cylinder with (C1)–(C5); A3: G_#X − F_#X = ∂H_#(cyl X) + H_#(cyl ∂X) via (C4)/(C5), and M(H_#(cyl X)) ≤ sup|G − F|(2Λ)^kM(X) via (C3), (L1), (L2).

A4: estimate (E) with a cut-off smooth homotopy; F_#X := lim(F_σ)_#X; mass, boundary, smooth case and identity, support, locality and linearity; Lipschitz homotopy formula by cut-off homotopies H_σ → H_*, weak limits and lower semicontinuity.
Definitions lpush := F_#X (Lipschitz F, NC X; 0 otherwise), cyl := sibling operator; verification of the twelve conjuncts incl. interface (6) via mollifiers and cut-off pull-backs.

subproblems.title: Countably rectifiable Borel sets are covered, up to a null set, by disjoint bi-Lipschitz images with injective derivative (parent B1; reused accepted dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces)
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ and every Borel, countably n-rectifiable M ⊆ ℝ^P there are maps F_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, Borel sets B_i ⊆ ℝⁿ and numbers m_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ) such that each F_i is Lipschitz, m_i|a − a'| ≤ |F_i(a) − F_i(a')| for a, a' ∈ B_i, F_i is differentiable with injective derivative at every point of B_i, the images F_i(B_i) are Borel subsets of M and pairwise disjoint, and μHE[n](M ∖ ⋃_i F_i(B_i)) = 0. This is the exact type of the accepted declaration dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces, reused verbatim.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)), MeasurableSet M → CountablyRectifiable n M → ∃ (F : ℕ → Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : ℕ → Set (Euclid n)) (m : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ i, ∃ L : NNReal, LipschitzWith L (F i)) ∧ (∀ i, MeasurableSet (B i)) ∧ (∀ i, 0 < m i) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ a ∈ B i, ∀ a' ∈ B i, m i * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖F i a - F i a'‖) ∧ (∀ i, ∀ a ∈ B i, DifferentiableAt ℝ (F i) a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ (F i) a)) ∧ (∀ i, MeasurableSet (F i '' B i)) ∧ (∀ i, F i '' B i ⊆ M) ∧ Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (F i '' B i) (F j '' B j)) ∧ μHE[n] (M \ ⋃ i, F i '' B i) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 7 (B1, Lipschitz parametrization of a countably rectifiable set), in the Borel form needed by this exact statement (the parent's final passage to compact pieces is not part of this statement and is omitted). This accepted declaration is reused verbatim; the proof below proves its exact statement. No hypotheses beyond those of the statement are used.

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; on ℝⁿ = Euclid n, Hⁿ = Lⁿ = volume (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume or the normalization of μHE). Lipschitz maps send Hⁿ-null sets to Hⁿ-null sets and Hⁿ(f(A)) ≤ Lip(f)ⁿHⁿ(A) (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le).

1. Rectifiable cover. By the definition of CountablyRectifiable n M there are M₀ with Hⁿ(M₀) = 0 and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ).

2. Differentiability. Fix j. D_j := {u : F_j is differentiable at u} is Borel (Mathlib measurableSet_of_differentiableAt) and its complement is Lⁿ-null (Rademacher, Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt), so Hⁿ(F_j(ℝⁿ ∖ D_j)) = 0.

3. Critical points. Z_j := {u ∈ D_j : DF_j(u) is not injective} is Borel (u ↦ DF_j(u) is Borel, Mathlib measurable_fderiv; non-injectivity is the vanishing of the continuous function A ↦ det(AᵀA)), and Hⁿ(F_j(Z_j)) = 0 by SimonGMT area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero (the image of the set of differentiability points with non-injective derivative is Hⁿ-null).

4. Approximately linear pieces. E_j := (D_j ∖ Z_j) ∩ F_j^{-1}(M) is Borel (M Borel, F_j continuous). For an injective linear A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P choose K_A > 0 with |Aw| ≥ |w|/K_A for all w (Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith or compactness of the unit sphere) and put r(A) := 1/(2K_A); put r(A) := 1 if A is not injective. F_j has derivative DF_j(u) at every u ∈ E_j, so Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt (f = F_j, s = E_j, f' = DF_j, r) gives pairwise disjoint Borel sets t_l (l ∈ ℕ) with E_j ⊆ ⋃_l t_l and linear maps A_l with |F_j(u) − F_j(v) − A_l(u − v)| ≤ r(A_l)|u − v| for u, v ∈ E_j ∩ t_l, and, if E_j ≠ ∅, A_l = DF_j(y_l) for some y_l ∈ E_j, so A_l is injective. Hence for u, v ∈ E_j ∩ t_l: |F_j(u) − F_j(v)| ≥ |A_l(u − v)| − r(A_l)|u − v| ≥ (1/K_{A_l} − 1/(2K_{A_l}))|u − v| = (2K_{A_l})^{-1}|u − v|. (If E_j = ∅ it contributes no pieces.)

5. Disjoint images. Enumerate the pairs (j, l) by i ∈ ℕ (Nat.pair) and put G_i := F_j, E_i := E_j ∩ t_l (Borel), κ_i := (2K_{A_l})^{-1} > 0 (κ_i := 1 for empty pieces). Define recursively B_i := E_i ∖ G_i^{-1}(⋃_{i'<i} G_{i'}(B_{i'})). By induction every G_{i'}(B_{i'}) is Borel: G_{i'} is continuous and injective on the Borel set B_{i'} ⊆ E_{i'} (injective by the lower bound of step 4), so its image is Borel by the Lusin–Souslin theorem (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn); hence B_i is Borel, and G_i(B_i) is Borel.

6. Properties. For each i: G_i is Lipschitz (it is some F_j); B_i is Borel; κ_i|a − a'| ≤ |G_i(a) − G_i(a')| for a, a' ∈ B_i ⊆ E_i; G_i is differentiable at every a ∈ B_i ⊆ D_j with injective derivative (B_i ∩ Z_j = ∅); G_i(B_i) is Borel; G_i(B_i) ⊆ G_i(E_j) ⊆ M. The images are pairwise disjoint: for i' < i, G_i(B_i) ∩ G_{i'}(B_{i'}) = ∅ by the definition of B_i. Finally, ⋃_{i' ≤ i} G_{i'}(B_{i'}) = ⋃_{i' ≤ i} G_{i'}(E_{i'}) for every i (induction: G_i(E_i) ⊆ G_i(B_i) ∪ ⋃_{i'<i} G_{i'}(B_{i'})), so ⋃_i G_i(B_i) = ⋃_i G_i(E_i) = ⋃_j F_j(E_j). If x ∈ M lies outside the Hⁿ-null set M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ ∖ D_j) ∪ ⋃_j F_j(Z_j), then x = F_j(u) for some j and u ∈ D_j ∖ Z_j, and u ∈ F_j^{-1}(M), i.e. u ∈ E_j, so x ∈ ⋃_i G_i(B_i). Hence Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_i G_i(B_i)) = 0 (countable subadditivity).

Taking F := G, B := B and m := κ gives all conjuncts of the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: Lipschitz cover M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃ F_j(ℝⁿ) from rectifiability.
Rademacher and the critical-set lemma remove null images of non-differentiability and critical points.
Approximately linear Borel partition with r(A) = 1/(2K_A) gives lower Lipschitz bounds.
Disjointify images with Lusin–Souslin; the union of images covers M up to a null set.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent planes of bi-Lipschitz pieces (parent B2; reused accepted ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae)

This is the exact type of the accepted declaration ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae, reused verbatim.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (F : Euclid n → Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (L : NNReal) (m : ℝ), LipschitzWith L F → MeasurableSet B → 0 < m → (∀ a ∈ B, ∀ a' ∈ B, m * ‖a - a'‖ ≤ ‖F a - F a'‖) → (∀ a ∈ B, DifferentiableAt ℝ F a ∧ Injective (fderiv ℝ F a)) → ∀ᵐ b ∂(volume.restrict B), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (F '' B) (F b) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ F b : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 8 (B2, approximate tangent planes of bi-Lipschitz pieces via the area formula and Lebesgue points), for a Borel piece B with injective derivative, exactly the statement used by the siblings. This accepted declaration is reused verbatim; the proof below proves its exact statement. No hypotheses beyond those of the statement are used.

Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n], equal to Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ. For a ∈ B put JF(a) := √det(DF(a)ᵀDF(a)) = √det(⟨DF(a)e_i, DF(a)e_j⟩); a ↦ JF(a) is Borel and 0 ≤ JF ≤ Lⁿ (‖DF‖ ≤ L). The area formula for a map that is Lipschitz and injective on a Borel set E ⊆ ℝⁿ: ∫_{F(E)} g dHⁿ = ∫_E g(F(a))·JF(a) da for Borel g ≥ 0 and for bounded Borel g with Hⁿ(F(E)) < ∞ (SimonGMT injective_area_formula_lipschitzOn / weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum, whose fibre sums are single terms for injective maps; the Jacobian of the within-derivative equals JF(a) at a.e. a ∈ E, where F is differentiable and E has density 1). blowUpMap x r y = r⁻¹(y − x).

1. Good points. By the Lebesgue density theorem (Mathlib Besicovitch.ae_tendsto_measure_inter_div_of_measurableSet) and the Lebesgue differentiation theorem for the bounded Borel function 1_B·JF (Mathlib IsUnifLocDoublingMeasure.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub), a.e. b ∈ B is a density point of B (Lⁿ(B ∩ B_ρ(b))/Lⁿ(B_ρ(b)) → 1) and a Lebesgue point of 1_B·JF (ρ^{−n}∫_{B_ρ(b)}|1_B JF − JF(b)| → 0). Fix such b; F is differentiable at b and V := DF(b)(ℝⁿ) has dimension n because DF(b) is injective, so finrank V = n.

2. Lower bound for the derivative. |DF(b)c| ≥ m|c| for all c ∈ ℝⁿ. Let |c| = 1 and ε ∈ (0, 1). Since b is a density point, for all small ρ the cone {a : |a − b| ≤ ρ, |(a − b)/|a − b| − c| < ε} meets B (it occupies a fixed positive fraction of B_ρ(b)); so there are a_k ∈ B, a_k → b, with |(a_k − b)/|a_k − b| − c| < ε. Then m|a_k − b| ≤ |F(a_k) − F(b)| = |DF(b)(a_k − b)| + o(|a_k − b|), so m ≤ |DF(b)c| + ‖DF(b)‖ε. Let ε → 0.

3. Rescaling. Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with spt f ⊆ B_R(0) and |f| ≤ K. Put x := F(b), F̃_r(c) := (F(b + rc) − x)/r and B_r := (B − b)/r for r > 0. Then blowUpMap x r '' F(B) = F̃_r(B_r); F̃_r is L-Lipschitz, |F̃_r(c) − F̃_r(c')| ≥ m|c − c'| on B_r (so F̃_r is injective on B_r and |F̃_r(c)| ≥ m|c| for c ∈ B_r, since 0 ∈ B_r), and JF̃_r(c) = JF(b + rc). F̃_r is Lipschitz and injective on the Borel set B_r, with DF̃_r(c) = DF(b + rc) wherever F is differentiable at b + rc, so the area formula for F̃_r on B_r gives
 ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' F(B)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{B_r} f(F̃_r(c))·JF(b + rc) dc = ∫ 1_B(b + rc)·f(F̃_r(c))·JF(b + rc) dc,
 and the integrand vanishes for |c| ≥ R/m (then |F̃_r(c)| ≥ R for c ∈ B_r).

4. Passage to the limit. On the ball Q := B_{R/m}(0): F̃_r(c) → DF(b)c uniformly as r ↓ 0 (differentiability at b), so f∘F̃_r → f∘DF(b) uniformly (f is uniformly continuous); and ∫_Q |1_B(b + rc)JF(b + rc) − JF(b)| dc = r^{−n}∫_{B_{rR/m}(b)}|1_B JF − JF(b)| → 0 (Lebesgue point; 1_B(b) = 1). Hence
 |∫_Q 1_B(b + rc) f(F̃_r(c)) JF(b + rc) dc − ∫_Q f(DF(b)c) JF(b) dc| ≤ Lⁿ∫_Q|f(F̃_r(c)) − f(DF(b)c)| dc + K∫_Q|1_B(b + rc)JF(b + rc) − JF(b)| dc → 0.

5. Identification of the limit. By step 2, f(DF(b)c) = 0 for |c| ≥ R/m, so ∫_Q f(DF(b)c)JF(b) dc = ∫_{ℝⁿ} f(DF(b)c)JF(b) dc = ∫_V f dHⁿ (area formula for the injective linear map DF(b), whose Jacobian is the constant JF(b)).

6. Steps 3–5 show ∫_{blowUpMap x r '' F(B)} f dHⁿ → ∫_V f dHⁿ as r ↓ 0 for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P); together with finrank V = n this is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n (F '' B) (F b) (LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ F b)), for a.e. b ∈ B (volume.restrict B). ∎
proof_key_steps: A.e. b ∈ B is a density point of B and a Lebesgue point of 1_B·JF.
At density points |DF(b)c| ≥ m|c|.
Area formula for the rescaled map F̃_r on (B − b)/r; the integrand vanishes for |c| ≥ R/m.
Uniform convergence F̃_r → DF(b) and the Lebesgue-point property give the limit ∫_V f dHⁿ.

subproblems.title: Weak continuity of pulled-back n-forms under uniform convergence with bounded Lipschitz constants (parent B4 lemma)
subproblems.statement: For n, N' ∈ ℕ, L ∈ ℝ≥0, L-Lipschitz maps H_j, H : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{N'} (j ∈ ℕ) with H_j → H uniformly on ℝⁿ, a Lebesgue integrable w : ℝⁿ → ℝ and a continuous, compactly supported n-form ω on ℝ^{N'}: ∫ w(u)·ω(H_j(u))(DH_j(u)e_1, …, DH_j(u)e_n) du → ∫ w(u)·ω(H(u))(DH(u)e_1, …, DH(u)e_n) du as j → ∞, where DK(u) = fderiv ℝ K u and e_a = EuclideanSpace.single a 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N' : ℕ) (L : NNReal) (Hs : ℕ → Euclid n → Euclid N') (H : Euclid n → Euclid N') (w : Euclid n → ℝ) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid N') n), (∀ j, LipschitzWith L (Hs j)) → LipschitzWith L H → TendstoUniformly Hs H atTop → Integrable w → Continuous ω → HasCompactSupport ω → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ u, w u * ω (Hs j u) (fun a => fderiv ℝ (Hs j) u (EuclideanSpace.single a 1))) atTop (𝓝 (∫ u, w u * ω (H u) (fun a => fderiv ℝ H u (EuclideanSpace.single a 1))))
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 10 (B4), the lemma on weak continuity of Jacobians, stated for globally Lipschitz maps; the only change is that ω may be any continuous compactly supported n-form (the proof never differentiates ω). No hypotheses and no sibling results are used.

Notation. e_1, …, e_n is the standard basis of ℝⁿ = Euclid n, du is Lebesgue measure (volume on Euclid n, which corresponds to the product Lebesgue measure on Fin n → ℝ, Mathlib PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp). For a map K : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{N'} write DK(u) := fderiv ℝ K u (= 0 where K is not differentiable) and Φ_K(u) := ω(K(u))(DK(u)e_1, …, DK(u)e_n). An L-Lipschitz map is differentiable Lⁿ-a.e. (Rademacher, Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt) with ‖DK(u)‖ ≤ L wherever it is differentiable, and u ↦ DK(u) is Borel (Mathlib measurable_fderiv). We must show ∫ w Φ_{H_j} du → ∫ w Φ_H du.

1. Bounds and measurability. C_ω := sup_y ‖ω(y)‖ < ∞ (operator norm of the continuous multilinear map ω(y); finite because ω is continuous with compact support). For every u, |Φ_K(u)| ≤ C_ω Π_a |DK(u)e_a| ≤ C_ω Lⁿ for K ∈ {H_j, H} (‖DK(u)‖ ≤ L, or DK(u) = 0). Φ_K is Borel (K continuous, ω continuous, DK Borel, evaluation continuous). Since w ∈ L¹, all integrals exist and |∫ w Φ_K| ≤ C_ωLⁿ‖w‖_{L¹}.

2. Case n = 0. Then Φ_K(u) = ω(K(u))() (no arguments). ω is uniformly continuous and H_j → H uniformly, so Φ_{H_j} → Φ_H uniformly, and |∫ w(Φ_{H_j} − Φ_H)| ≤ ‖w‖_{L¹} sup|Φ_{H_j} − Φ_H| → 0. From now on n ≥ 1.

3. Reduction to smooth compactly supported w. Given ε > 0 choose w̃ ∈ C^∞_c(ℝⁿ) with ‖w − w̃‖_{L¹} < ε (density of C^∞_c in L¹). By step 1, |∫(w − w̃)Φ_K| ≤ C_ωLⁿε for every K ∈ {H_j, H}, uniformly in j. Hence it suffices to prove the claim for w ∈ C^∞_c(ℝⁿ).

4. Expansion in minors. Let e'_1, …, e'_{N'} be the standard basis of ℝ^{N'}. Expanding each argument z_b = Σ_c (z_b)_c e'_c by multilinearity and using alternation (terms with a repeated index vanish; an injective index map is uniquely J∘σ with J strictly increasing and σ a permutation), ω(y)(z_1, …, z_n) = Σ_J ω_J(y)·det[(z_b)_{J(a)}]_{a,b}, the sum over strictly increasing J : Fin n → Fin N', with ω_J(y) := ω(y)(e'_{J(1)}, …, e'_{J(n)}), a continuous compactly supported function. At every point u where K is differentiable, (z_b)_{J(a)} = ∂_bK^{J(a)}(u), so Φ_K(u) = Σ_J ω_J(K(u))·det DK^J(u), where K^J := (K^{J(1)}, …, K^{J(n)}) : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ is L-Lipschitz (a coordinate projection has norm ≤ 1); this identity holds Lⁿ-a.e. It therefore suffices to show, for one fixed J, ∫ w·ω_J(H_j)·det DH_j^J du → ∫ w·ω_J(H)·det DH^J du.

5. Splitting. ∫ wω_J(H_j)det DH_j^J − ∫ wω_J(H)det DH^J = ∫ w(ω_J(H_j) − ω_J(H))det DH_j^J + ∫ wω_J(H)(det DH_j^J − det DH^J). For a square matrix A, |det A| ≤ ‖A‖ⁿ (Hadamard), so |det DH_j^J| ≤ Lⁿ a.e.; ω_J is uniformly continuous, so ω_J∘H_j → ω_J∘H uniformly, and the first term is at most ‖w‖_{L¹}Lⁿ sup|ω_J∘H_j − ω_J∘H| → 0. For the second term put c := w·(ω_J∘H) ∈ C_c(ℝⁿ), v_j := H_j^J, v := H^J; these are L-Lipschitz maps ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with v_j → v uniformly, so step 6 shows ∫ c det Dv_j → ∫ c det Dv.

6. Claim: for c ∈ C_c(ℝⁿ) and L-Lipschitz v_j, v : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ with v_j → v uniformly, ∫ c·det Dv_j du → ∫ c·det Dv du.
 For a Lipschitz function g put dg := Σ_b ∂_bg dx^b (a.e. partial derivatives, bounded and measurable); for bounded measurable compactly supported coefficients, identify an n-form f dx^1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^n with f for integration. Concretely, for an (n − r)-form β = Σ_I β_I dx^I (I increasing of length n − r) the n-form β ∧ dv^{a_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dv^{a_r} is (Σ_I ±β_I·det[∂_{b}v^{a_m}]_{m ≤ r, b ∉ I}) dx^1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^n, with the r×r minors of the matrix of a.e. partial derivatives taken on the complementary columns and the sign of the shuffle (I, I^c); all statements below are statements about these coordinate integrals, and the exterior-algebra notation is only bookkeeping for them. Prove by induction on r = 0, …, n the statement (P_r): for every continuous compactly supported (n − r)-form β on ℝⁿ and all a_1, …, a_r ∈ {1, …, n}, ∫ β ∧ dv_j^{a_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dv_j^{a_r} → ∫ β ∧ dv^{a_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dv^{a_r}. The claim is (P_n) with β = c and a = (1, …, n), because c·dv^1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dv^n = c·det Dv·dx^1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^n.
 (P_0) holds trivially (no dependence on j). Assume (P_{r−1}) with r ≥ 1.
 (i) Integration by parts for Lipschitz functions: for β ∈ C^∞_c (an (n − r)-form) and Lipschitz g, u_2, …, u_r: ∫ β ∧ dg ∧ du_2 ∧ ⋯ ∧ du_r = (−1)^{n−r+1}∫ g dβ ∧ du_2 ∧ ⋯ ∧ du_r. For C^∞ functions this is ∫ d(gβ ∧ du_2 ∧ ⋯ ∧ du_r) = 0 (Stokes for a compactly supported exact n-form, i.e. ∫∂_b(·) = 0 for compactly supported C^1 coefficients), together with d(gβ ∧ du_2 ∧ ⋯ ∧ du_r) = dg ∧ β ∧ du_2 ∧ ⋯ + g dβ ∧ du_2 ∧ ⋯ (d(du_i) = 0) and dg ∧ β = (−1)^{n−r}β ∧ dg. For Lipschitz functions mollify g and all u_i simultaneously: for each Lipschitz h, h∗ϕ_δ → h uniformly, D(h∗ϕ_δ) = (Dh)∗ϕ_δ (the a.e. derivative of a Lipschitz function is its weak derivative, Mathlib LipschitzWith.integral_lineDeriv_mul_eq) → Dh a.e. (Mathlib ContDiffBump.ae_convolution_tendsto_right_of_locallyIntegrable) and |D(h∗ϕ_δ)| ≤ Lip(h); dominated convergence on the compact set spt β gives the identity in the limit.
 (ii) Smooth β. With R_j := dv_j^{a_2} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dv_j^{a_r} and R := dv^{a_2} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dv^{a_r}, (i) gives ∫ β ∧ dv_j^{a_1} ∧ R_j − ∫ β ∧ dv^{a_1} ∧ R = ±[∫(v_j^{a_1} − v^{a_1}) dβ ∧ R_j + ∫ v^{a_1} dβ ∧ (R_j − R)]. The first integral is at most sup|v_j − v|·C_β·(C_nL)^{r−1}·Lⁿ(spt β) → 0 (the coefficients of R_j are sums of products of r − 1 partial derivatives, each bounded by L). The second tends to 0 by (P_{r−1}) applied to the continuous compactly supported (n − r + 1)-form v^{a_1}dβ.
 (iii) Continuous β. Given ε > 0 choose a smooth β̃ with support in a fixed compact K ⊇ spt β and sup|β − β̃| < ε (mollification). Then |∫(β − β̃) ∧ dv_j^{a_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ dv_j^{a_r}| ≤ ε·C_n·L^r·Lⁿ(K) uniformly in j, and the same bound holds with v in place of v_j; with (ii) for β̃ this gives (P_r).
 This completes the induction and proves the claim.

7. Conclusion. By steps 3–6 (and step 2 for n = 0), ∫ w(u)·ω(H_j(u))(DH_j(u)e_1, …, DH_j(u)e_n) du → ∫ w(u)·ω(H(u))(DH(u)e_1, …, DH(u)e_n) du; in Lean the vectors DH(u)e_a are fderiv ℝ H u (EuclideanSpace.single a 1). ∎
proof_key_steps: Uniform bound |Φ_K| ≤ C_ωLⁿ; the case n = 0 by uniform convergence.
Reduce to w ∈ C^∞_c by L¹ density.
Expand ω in the minors det DH^J with continuous coefficients ω_J; uniform convergence handles ω_J∘H_j.
Induction (P_r) on wedge factors with integration by parts for Lipschitz functions (mollification) gives ∫ c det Dv_j → ∫ c det Dv.

Source: parent proof, Part B: the normalization preamble, steps 7–10 (B1 parametrization, B2/B2′ tangent planes and orientations of pieces, B3 the integer multiplicity current Φ_F closed by IMS, B4 identification F_#X = Φ_F via weak continuity of Jacobians; Simon Ch. 6, 3.3–3.9). The push-forward enters only through the hypothesis on S (the interface (6) of the sibling dimred_mbl_dt_lp_pushforward_operators). Siblings used: dimred_mbl_dt_lp_covector_bounds ((L1)), covectorEuclideanNorm_gram_bounds ((L3): |α(v)| ≤ |α|√det Gram(v)), dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces (B1), ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae (B2), dimred_mbl_dt_lp_jacobian_weak_continuity (B4 lemma). (VO), (MR), (IMC) = ((a) locality of approximate tangent spaces, (b) restriction to a Borel set, (c) differences, (d) |R.orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e. on the carrier) and (IMS) are the antecedents; (IMS) is used after discharging its own antecedents (VO), (MR), (IMC).

Notation. n := k + 1 ≥ 1, Hⁿ := μHE[n] (= Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ = Euclid n), e = (e_1, …, e_n) the standard basis of ℝⁿ. For linear A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^m, JA := √det(⟨Ae_a, Ae_b⟩)_{a,b} (= SimonGMT's normDet). For a Lipschitz map K : ℝⁿ → ℝ^m, DK(u) := fderiv ℝ K u (K is differentiable a.e., Rademacher), JK(u) := J(DK(u)), and for an n-form ω, (K^#ω)(e)(u) := ω(K(u))(DK(u)e_1, …, DK(u)e_n). |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α, ‖ω‖ := sup_y|ω(y)|. Lⁿ := volume.
 (AF) Area formula: if K is Lipschitz and injective on a Borel set E ⊆ ℝⁿ, then ∫_{K(E)} g dHⁿ = ∫_E g(K(u))JK(u) du for Borel g ≥ 0 (SimonGMT injective_area_formula_lipschitzOn, weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum, whose fibre sums are single terms for an injective map; the within-derivative Jacobian equals JK(u) at a.e. u ∈ E). It extends to g ≥ 0 that is merely Hⁿ⌞K(E)-a.e. measurable (change g on a null set; by (NT) below the corresponding u-set is null), and then to real g with ∫_{K(E)}|g| dHⁿ < ∞ by splitting g = g⁺ − g⁻: ∫_{K(E)} g dHⁿ = ∫_E g(K(u))JK(u) du, both sides finite. This is how (AF) is applied below to integrands involving ξ, which is only a.e. strongly measurable.
 (NT) Null-set transfer: if K is Lipschitz, E Borel and κ|u − v| ≤ |K(u) − K(v)| for u, v ∈ E (κ > 0), then for Z ⊆ E, Lⁿ(Z) ≤ κ^{−n}Hⁿ(K(Z)) (the inverse K(E) → E is κ^{−1}-Lipschitz; Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le), and Hⁿ(K(Z)) ≤ Lip(K)ⁿLⁿ(Z). Hence a property holding Hⁿ-a.e. on K(E) holds at K(u) for Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ E, the image of an Lⁿ-null subset of E is Hⁿ-null, and K pushes Lⁿ⌞E to a measure absolutely continuous with respect to Hⁿ⌞K(E) (and conversely). Also, by (AF), Lⁿ(Z) ≤ κ^{−n}∫_Z JK for Borel Z ⊆ E, so JK ≥ κⁿ Lⁿ-a.e. on E.

0. Linear algebra.
 (0a) |α(v_1, …, v_n)| ≤ |α|·√det(⟨v_a, v_b⟩) (sibling gram_bounds, first conjunct); in particular |(K^#ω)(e)(u)| ≤ |ω(K(u))|·JK(u).

With C_{ab} := ⟨τ_a, Ae_b⟩, Ae_b = Σ_a C_{ab}τ_a, so α(Ae) = det(C)·α(τ) for every n-covector α (multilinearity and alternation), and (⟨Ae_a, Ae_b⟩) = CᵀC, so |det C| = JA > 0. Consequently, if ξ is a unit orientation of A(ℝⁿ) (ξ(α) = ±α(τ) for all α), then JA·ξ(α) = s·α(Ae) for all α with a sign s ∈ {1, −1} independent of α; and the n-vector α ↦ α(Ae)/JA equals ±(α ↦ α(τ)), i.e. it is a unit orientation of A(ℝⁿ) in the sense of IsUnitOrientationOf.
 (0c) If A : ℝ^N → ℝ^{N'} is linear and ω an n-covector on ℝ^{N'}, then |ω∘A^{×n}| ≤ ‖A‖ⁿ|ω| (sibling covector_bounds, (L1)).
 (0d) If A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^m, B : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{m'} are linear, B injective and |Aw| ≤ Λ|Bw| for all w, then JA ≤ ΛⁿJB: AᵀA ≤ Λ²BᵀB as quadratic forms; with Q := BᵀB > 0, det(AᵀA) = det(Q)·det(Q^{−1/2}AᵀAQ^{−1/2}) and the middle matrix is symmetric with eigenvalues in [0, Λ²].
 (0e) The zero current of 𝒟_n(ℝ^m) is integer multiplicity: the IMRep with empty carrier, multiplicity 0 and orientation 0 satisfies all conditions vacuously (μHE[n] ∅ = 0, so the carrier is rectifiable by countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero), and its action is an integral over ∅, i.e. 0.

1. Normalization (parent Part B preamble). Let R₀ = (M₀, θ, ξ) represent X. E := spt X is closed, hence Borel. By (IMC)(b) (U = ℝ^N open) there are a current A and an IMRep R with R.Represents A, carrier M := M₀ ∩ E, multiplicity θ and orientation ξ. Hⁿ(M₀ ∖ E) = 0: by (MR) for X, R₀ and the open set W := ℝ^N ∖ E, ∫_{M₀∖E} θ dHⁿ = R₀.measure(W) = M_W(X), and M_W(X) = 0 because every admissible form with tsupport ⊆ W is disjoint from spt X, hence killed by (VO); as θ ≥ 1 on M₀, Hⁿ(M₀ ∖ E) = 0. Therefore μHE[n].restrict M₀ = μHE[n].restrict M, so A(ω) = R.action(ω) = R₀.action(ω) = X(ω) for all ω, i.e. R represents X. So X = τ(M, θ, ξ) with M ⊆ spt X Borel and countably n-rectifiable, ∫_M θ dHⁿ = R.measure(ℝ^N) = M(X) < ∞ ((MR) with W = ℝ^N), Hⁿ(M) ≤ M(X) (θ ≥ 1), X(η) = ∫_M θ·ξ(η) dHⁿ for every test form η, and |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M ((IMC)(d)).

2. B1 (sibling dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces applied to M). There are Lipschitz G_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N (constants L_i), Borel A_i ⊆ ℝⁿ and m_i > 0 (i ∈ ℕ) with: m_i|u − v| ≤ |G_i(u) − G_i(v)| on A_i; G_i differentiable with DG_i(u) injective at every u ∈ A_i; G_i(A_i) Borel, ⊆ M, pairwise disjoint; Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_i G_i(A_i)) = 0. Put θ_i := θ∘G_i (Borel, ≥ 1 on A_i). By (AF) and disjointness, Σ_i ∫_{A_i} θ_i JG_i du = Σ_i ∫_{G_i(A_i)} θ dHⁿ = ∫_M θ dHⁿ = M(X); by (NT), JG_i ≥ m_iⁿ a.e. on A_i, so ∫_{A_i} θ_i du ≤ m_i^{−n}∫_{G_i(A_i)} θ dHⁿ < ∞.

3. B2′ (tangent planes and orientation on the pieces). Proof: by the sibling ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae (G_i, A_i, L_i, m_i), for a.e. u ∈ A_i the set G_i(A_i) has approximate tangent space V_i(u) at G_i(u). By (IMC)(a) (U = ℝ^N; G_i(A_i) ⊆ M both Borel; Hⁿ(M ∩ K) ≤ Hⁿ(M) < ∞), for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ G_i(A_i) the approximate tangent spaces of G_i(A_i) and of M at x coincide; by (NT) this holds at x = G_i(u) for a.e. u ∈ A_i. The IMRep property (orients) gives, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, a plane Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q; by (NT) this holds at x = G_i(u) for a.e. u ∈ A_i, and by uniqueness (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) Q = V_i(u). Then (0b) with A = DG_i(u) gives the sign s_i(u). Put s_i(u) := 1 at the remaining (null) points of A_i. Measurability: on the good set, s_i(u) = ξ(G_i(u))(γ_u)/JG_i(u), where γ_u(w) := det(⟨DG_i(u)e_a, w_b⟩)_{a,b} is an n-covector depending Borel-measurably on u with γ_u(DG_i(u)e) = JG_i(u)²; since ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M and G_i pushes Lⁿ⌞A_i to a measure ≪ Hⁿ⌞M (NT), u ↦ ξ(G_i(u)) is a.e. strongly measurable for Lⁿ⌞A_i, so s_i is Lⁿ⌞A_i-a.e. measurable. Hence w_i := θ_i s_i 1_{A_i} ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ) (step 2).

4. Setup. H_i := F∘G_i is ΛL_i-Lipschitz. At a.e. u ∈ A_i, H_i is differentiable (Rademacher) and |DH_i(u)w| = lim_{t↓0}|F(G_i(u + tw)) − F(G_i(u))|/t ≤ Λ|DG_i(u)w|, so JH_i(u) ≤ ΛⁿJG_i(u) by (0d). For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^{N'}) define Φ(ω) := Σ_i ∫_{A_i} θ_i s_i (H_i^#ω)(e) du. By (0a), |(H_i^#ω)(e)| ≤ ‖ω‖JH_i ≤ Λⁿ‖ω‖JG_i a.e. on A_i, so the series converges absolutely and |Φ(ω)| ≤ ΛⁿM(X)‖ω‖.

 (a) A_i^+ := {u ∈ A_i : H_i differentiable at u, DH_i(u) injective} is Borel (Mathlib measurableSet_of_differentiableAt, measurable_fderiv; non-injectivity is the vanishing of the continuous function A ↦ det(AᵀA)). At points of A_i ∖ A_i^+ where H_i is differentiable, (H_i^#ω)(e) = 0 (the vectors DH_i(u)e_a are dependent), and the non-differentiability points are null; so Φ(ω) = Σ_i ∫_{A_i^+} θ_i s_i (H_i^#ω)(e) du. Partition A_i^+ into bi-Lipschitz pieces: for an injective linear A : ℝⁿ → ℝ^{N'} choose K_A > 0 with |Aw| ≥ |w|/K_A for all w (Mathlib LinearMap.exists_antilipschitzWith) and put r(A) := 1/(2K_A); put r(A) := 1 if A is not injective (so r is ℝ≥0-valued and never 0). H_i has derivative DH_i(u) at every u ∈ A_i^+, so Mathlib exists_partition_approximatesLinearOn_of_hasFDerivWithinAt (f = H_i, s = A_i^+, f' = DH_i, r) gives pairwise disjoint Borel sets t_l with A_i^+ ⊆ ⋃_l t_l and linear maps B_l with |H_i(u) − H_i(v) − B_l(u − v)| ≤ r(B_l)|u − v| for u, v ∈ A_i^+ ∩ t_l and, if A_i^+ ≠ ∅, B_l = DH_i(y_l) for some y_l ∈ A_i^+ (so B_l is injective). Put A_{il} := A_i^+ ∩ t_l (Borel, pairwise disjoint, union A_i^+) and κ_{il} := (2K_{B_l})^{−1}; then |H_i(u) − H_i(v)| ≥ |B_l(u − v)| − r(B_l)|u − v| ≥ κ_{il}|u − v| for u, v ∈ A_{il}; in particular H_i is injective on A_{il}.
 (b) For each (i, l) let N_{il} := H_i(A_{il}) (Borel by Lusin–Souslin, Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn), h_{il} := (H_i|A_{il})^{−1} : N_{il} → A_{il}, and define R_{il}: carrier N_{il}; multiplicity μ_{il}(y) := θ_i(h_{il}(y)) for y ∈ N_{il} and 0 otherwise; orientation ζ_{il}(y) := s_i(h_{il}(y))·(α ↦ α(DH_i(h_{il}y)e)/JH_i(h_{il}y)) for y ∈ N_{il} and 0 otherwise. R_{il} is an IMRep in U = ℝ^{N'}: the carrier is Borel and countably n-rectifiable (contained in the range of the Lipschitz H_i; SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_range, CountablyRectifiable.mono); the multiplicity is ℕ-valued, Borel ({y ∈ N_{il} : μ_{il}(y) = m} = H_i({u ∈ A_{il} : θ_i(u) = m}) is Borel by Lusin–Souslin) and ≥ 1 on N_{il}; it is integrable: ∫_{N_{il}} μ_{il} dHⁿ = ∫_{A_{il}} θ_i JH_i du ≤ Λⁿ∫_{A_i} θ_i JG_i du < ∞ ((AF) for H_i on A_{il}); the orientation is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞N_{il} (h_{il} pushes Hⁿ⌞N_{il} to a measure ≪ Lⁿ⌞A_{il} by (NT), and s_i, DH_i, JH_i are a.e. measurable on A_{il}); and it orients: by the sibling ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae (H_i, A_{il}, ΛL_i, κ_{il}; H_i is differentiable with injective derivative on A_{il} ⊆ A_i^+), for a.e. u ∈ A_{il} the set N_{il} has approximate tangent space DH_i(u)(ℝⁿ) at H_i(u), and by (0b) ζ_{il}(H_i(u)) = ±(α ↦ α(τ)) for an orthonormal basis τ of that plane, i.e. IsUnitOrientationOf (ζ_{il}(H_i u)) (DH_i(u)(ℝⁿ)); the exceptional u form an Lⁿ-null set with Hⁿ-null image (NT).
 (c) By (IMC)(b) (U = E = ℝ^{N'}) there are a current Φ_{il} ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^{N'}) and an IMRep with the carrier, multiplicity and orientation of R_{il} representing it; so Φ_{il} is integer multiplicity and, by (AF) (the integrand is bounded by μ_{il}‖ω‖ by (0a), hence integrable), Φ_{il}(ω) = ∫_{N_{il}} μ_{il}ζ_{il}(ω) dHⁿ = ∫_{A_{il}} θ_i s_i [ω(H_i(u))(DH_i(u)e)/JH_i(u)]·JH_i(u) du = ∫_{A_{il}} θ_i s_i (H_i^#ω)(e) du. By (MR), M(Φ_{il}) = R_{il}.measure(ℝ^{N'}) = ∫_{A_{il}} θ_i JH_i du, so Σ_{i,l} M(Φ_{il}) ≤ ΛⁿM(X) < ∞.
 (d) Enumerate the pairs (i, l) by m ∈ ℕ and put W_m := Φ_{i_m l_m}, padding with zero currents (integer multiplicity by (0e)) if there are finitely many. Σ_m M(W_m) < ∞, so (IMS) (with P := N' and this k) gives an integer multiplicity Ŝ ∈ 𝒟_{k+1}(ℝ^{N'}) with HasSum (m ↦ W_m(ω)) (Ŝ(ω)) for every ω. The double series Σ_i Σ_l ∫_{A_{il}} θ_i s_i (H_i^#ω)(e) du converges absolutely (bound ‖ω‖∫_{A_{il}} θ_iJH_i), so it may be reordered: Ŝ(ω) = Σ_i ∫_{A_i^+} θ_i s_i (H_i^#ω)(e) du = Φ(ω).

6. B4 (identification: S = Φ). Let F_j and, for a fixed ω, η_j be as in the hypothesis: F_j is C^∞ and Λ-Lipschitz (so ‖DF_j‖ ≤ Λ), F_j → F uniformly, η_j = F_j^#ω on an open W_j ⊇ spt X, and X(η_j) → S(ω). By step 1 and M ⊆ spt X ⊆ W_j, X(η_j) = ∫_M θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(F_j(x))∘DF_j(x)^{×n}) dHⁿ(x). The integrand is bounded by θ·Λⁿ‖ω‖ a.e. ((IMC)(d), (0c)), hence integrable; splitting M into the disjoint G_i(A_i) and a null set and applying (AF) for G_i on A_i, step 3 (with α := ω(F_j(G_i u))∘DF_j(G_i u)^{×n}) and the chain rule DH_{ij}(u) = DF_j(G_i(u))∘DG_i(u) for H_{ij} := F_j∘G_i at every u ∈ A_i:
 X(η_j) = Σ_i ∫_{A_i} θ_i(u)JG_i(u)ξ(G_i(u))(ω(F_j(G_i u))∘DF_j(G_i u)^{×n}) du = Σ_i ∫_{A_i} θ_i s_i (H_{ij}^#ω)(e) du = Σ_i ∫ w_i·ω(H_{ij}(u))(DH_{ij}(u)e) du.
 For fixed i, the maps H_{ij} (j ∈ ℕ) and H_i are ΛL_i-Lipschitz, H_{ij} → H_i uniformly (|F_j∘G_i − F∘G_i| ≤ sup|F_j − F|), w_i ∈ L¹(ℝⁿ) (step 3), and ω is continuous with compact support; so the sibling dimred_mbl_dt_lp_jacobian_weak_continuity gives ∫ w_i·ω(H_{ij})(DH_{ij}e) → ∫ w_i·ω(H_i)(DH_ie) = ∫_{A_i} θ_i s_i (H_i^#ω)(e) du as j → ∞. The i-th term is bounded in absolute value by Λⁿ‖ω‖∫_{A_i} θ_i JG_i du (by the first expression and (0c), |ξ| ≤ |·|), which is summable in i with sum ΛⁿM(X)‖ω‖. By dominated convergence for series (Mathlib tendsto_tsum_of_dominated_convergence), X(η_j) → Σ_i ∫_{A_i} θ_i s_i (H_i^#ω)(e) du = Φ(ω).

7. Conclusion. For every ω, S(ω) = lim_j X(η_j) = Φ(ω) = Ŝ(ω) (uniqueness of limits, steps 5 and 6), so S = Ŝ (GeometricCurrentOn.ext), and S is integer multiplicity. ∎

2. Pieces and tangent planes of M. Apply the sibling dpf_rectifiable_bilipschitz_pieces to M (Borel, countably n-rectifiable): Lipschitz G_i : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N, Borel A_i, m_i > 0 with m_i|u − v| ≤ |G_i(u) − G_i(v)| on A_i, G_i differentiable with injective derivative on A_i, G_i(A_i) Borel, ⊆ M, pairwise disjoint, Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_i G_i(A_i)) = 0. Put V_i(u) := DG_i(u)(ℝⁿ). Claim: for Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ A_i, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M (G_i u) V_i(u) and ξ(G_i(u)) = ±(α ↦ α(τ)) for an orthonormal basis τ of V_i(u). Proof: by the sibling ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae, for a.e. u ∈ A_i the set G_i(A_i) has approximate tangent space V_i(u) at G_i(u); by (IMC)(a) (U = ℝ^N, G_i(A_i) ⊆ M Borel, Hⁿ(M) < ∞) and (NT), the approximate tangent spaces of G_i(A_i) and M coincide at G_i(u) for a.e. u ∈ A_i; the IMRep property (orients) and (NT) give, for a.e. u ∈ A_i, Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M (G_i u) Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(G_i u)) Q, and uniqueness (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique) gives Q = V_i(u).

3. Product-null lemma. If Z ⊆ ℝ^N has Hⁿ(Z) = 0 and I ⊆ ℝ is a bounded interval, then H^{n+1}(ι(I × Z)) = 0. μHE[d] is a positive constant multiple of μH[d], so it suffices to show μH[n+1](ι(I × Z)) = 0. Given ε ∈ (0, 1), cover Z by sets C_j (j ≥ 1) with Σ_j (diam C_j)ⁿ < ε and put d_j := max(diam C_j, ε·2^{−j}), so 0 < d_j ≤ max(ε^{1/n}, ε) < 1 and Σ_j d_jⁿ < 2ε. Cover I × C_j by at most |I|/d_j + 1 sets [a, a + d_j] × C_j, each of diameter ≤ √2·d_j. The sum of the (n+1)-st powers of the diameters is ≤ Σ_j(|I|/d_j + 1)(√2d_j)^{n+1} ≤ 2^{(n+1)/2}(|I| + 1)Σ_j d_jⁿ < 2^{(n+3)/2}(|I| + 1)ε, and all covering sets have diameter ≤ √2·max(ε^{1/n}, ε) → 0. Hence μH[n+1](I × Z) = 0 in ℝ × ℝ^N, and ι is an isometry.

4. Product pieces. Ĝ_i : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ^{N+1}, Ĝ_i(z) := ι(z_0, G_i(tail z)), and Â_i := {z : z_0 ∈ (0, 1), tail z ∈ A_i} (Borel). Ĝ_i is Lipschitz; for z, z' ∈ Â_i, |Ĝ_i(z) − Ĝ_i(z')|² = |z_0 − z'_0|² + |G_i(tail z) − G_i(tail z')|² ≥ min(1, m_i)²|z − z'|²; Ĝ_i is differentiable at every z ∈ Â_i with DĜ_i(z)(s, w) = s·e₀ + J(DG_i(tail z)w), which is injective, DĜ_i(z)(ℝ^{n+1}) = ℝe₀ ⊕ J(V_i(tail z)), and JĜ_i(z) = JG_i(tail z) (the Gram matrix is block diagonal diag(1, Gram(DG_i(tail z)e))).

5. Product formula. M̃ := {y : y_0 ∈ (0, 1), tail y ∈ M} = ι((0, 1) × M) is Borel. For Borel f ≥ 0 on ℝ^{N+1}: ∫_{M̃} f dH^{n+1} = ∫_0^1 ∫_M f(ι(t, x)) dHⁿ(x) dt. Proof: M̃ is the disjoint union of the sets Ĝ_i(Â_i) = ι((0, 1) × G_i(A_i)) and ι((0, 1) × Z), Z := M ∖ ⋃_i G_i(A_i); the last set is H^{n+1}-null by step 3, and Hⁿ(Z) = 0 makes it irrelevant on the right side too. For each i, by (AF) for Ĝ_i on Â_i, Fubini (Lebesgue measure on ℝ^{n+1} is the product of the Lebesgue measures of z_0 and tail z: Mathlib PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp and MeasureTheory.volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove) and (AF) for G_i on A_i: ∫_{Ĝ_i(Â_i)} f dH^{n+1} = ∫_{Â_i} f(Ĝ_i(z))JG_i(tail z) dz = ∫_0^1 ∫_{A_i} f(ι(t, G_i(u)))JG_i(u) du dt = ∫_0^1 ∫_{G_i(A_i)} f(ι(t, x)) dHⁿ(x) dt. Summing over i (monotone convergence) gives the formula. Equivalently, Ψ(t, x) := ι(t, x) sends (L¹⌞(0, 1)) ⊗ (Hⁿ⌞M) to H^{n+1}⌞M̃ (equality of measures on Borel sets), so the formula also holds for every f integrable for either measure, and a.e. statements and a.e. strong measurability transfer along Ψ and along tail. In particular H^{n+1}(M̃) = Hⁿ(M) < ∞ and ∫_{M̃} θ∘tail dH^{n+1} = ∫_M θ dHⁿ = M(X) < ∞.

6. The IMRep R̃. Carrier M̃ ⊆ ℝ^{N+1} (Borel); multiplicity θ̃(y) := θ(tail y) (Borel, ℕ-valued, ≥ 1 on M̃; extend by the same formula, which is still Borel); orientation ξ̃(y) := ξ(tail y)∘(α ↦ α₁), a continuous linear functional on (n+1)-covectors. ξ̃ is a.e. strongly measurable for H^{n+1}⌞M̃: by step 5 with f = g∘tail, tail pushes H^{n+1}⌞M̃ forward to Hⁿ⌞M, ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M, and α ↦ α₁ is a fixed continuous linear map. Rectifiability: M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝⁿ) (Hⁿ(M₀) = 0, F_j Lipschitz) gives M̃ ⊆ ι((0, 1) × M₀) ∪ ⋃_j F̃_j(ℝ^{n+1}) with F̃_j(z) := ι(z_0, F_j(tail z)) Lipschitz, and the first set is H^{n+1}-null by step 3. Local integrability of θ̃ follows from step 5. Orientation: fix i. By the sibling ptd_piece_image_approxTangent_ae applied to Ĝ_i on Â_i (degree n + 1), for a.e. z ∈ Â_i the set Ĝ_i(Â_i) has approximate tangent space ℝe₀ ⊕ J(V_i(tail z)) at Ĝ_i(z); by (IMC)(a) (U = ℝ^{N+1}, Ĝ_i(Â_i) ⊆ M̃ Borel, H^{n+1}(M̃) < ∞) and (NT) for Ĝ_i on Â_i, the same holds for M̃ at Ĝ_i(z) for a.e. z ∈ Â_i. By step 2 and Fubini (the set {z ∈ Â_i : tail z ∈ Z'} has Lebesgue measure 0 when Lⁿ(Z') = 0), for a.e. z ∈ Â_i also ξ(G_i(tail z)) = ±(β ↦ β(τ)) with τ an orthonormal basis of V_i(tail z). For such z and y := Ĝ_i(z) = ι(z_0, G_i(tail z)): ξ̃(y)(α) = ξ(G_i(tail z))(α₁) = ±α₁(τ) = ±α(e₀, Jτ_1, …, Jτ_n), and (e₀, Jτ_1, …, Jτ_n) is an orthonormal basis of ℝe₀ ⊕ J(V_i(tail z)); so IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ̃ y) (ℝe₀ ⊕ J(V_i(tail z))) and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt (n+1) M̃ y (ℝe₀ ⊕ J(V_i(tail z))). The exceptional points form an H^{n+1}-null set: images of Lebesgue-null subsets of Â_i under Ĝ_i are null (NT), and ι((0, 1) × Z) is null (step 3). Hence (M̃, θ̃, ξ̃) is an IMRep in U = ℝ^{N+1}.

((IMC)(d) and |α₁| ≤ |α|), which is integrable with integral ≤ M(X)‖ω‖. By Fubini and step 5 (applied to the integrable function θ̃·ξ̃(ω) on M̃):

 Hence R̃ represents C, so C is integer multiplicity. ∎
